Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaCorp Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing up will be given at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NovaCorp's Q3 2024 results. With me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Marketing Officer; Morgan Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Riley Chen, Chief Innovation Officer; Casey Lopez, Chief Sales Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. NovaCorp delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover overall financial performance, brand performance and innovation, supply chain and operational efficiency, marketing and promotional activities, sustainability initiatives, digital transformation, sales performance and channel strategy, and outlook for the remainder of the year.

I will now turn the call over to Jordan Lee to provide more detail on our financial results.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $15.2 billion, representing a 6% increase reported and 5.2% organic growth compared to the prior year—well ahead of our guided range and accelerating from the 3.8% we posted in Q2. This marks our sixth consecutive quarter of positive organic growth amid a still-challenging macroeconomic backdrop, including persistent inflation in key input costs like cocoa, palm oil, and PET resin, which are up 15-20% year-over-year across our supply chain.

Gross margin was 51.2%, up 150 basis points year-over-year and 80 basis points sequentially from Q2, driven by pricing actions, mix management, productivity savings, and some input cost relief. This is our sixth straight quarter of expansion, with a trailing four-quarter average of 50.8%, above our 49-51% long-term target and competitive with peers like Procter & Gamble around 50% and Unilever in the mid-40s. Operating income was $2.8 billion, up 14%, and adjusted diluted earnings per share were $1.45, up 12% on a constant currency basis. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives, with free cash flow at $2.1 billion, up 15% year-over-year.

Let me unpack our organic sales growth decomposition first, as it gives a clear line of sight into the health of our brands and commercial strategies. We break it into volume, pricing, and mix. Volume grew 1.8%, up 110 basis points sequentially—our strongest since Q4 2022—thanks to our Volume Momentum Initiative with targeted in-store activations and shopper marketing in high-velocity channels like Walmart, Costco, and Sam's Club, expanding household penetration by 2.3 points in North America. By segment: Snacks & Confectionery at 35% of sales saw +2.5% volume from reformulated NutriCrunch bars tapping better-for-you trends, gaining 1.2 share points versus Mondelez's Oreo Thins per Nielsen; Beverages at 25% were flat overall but +4.1% in functional waters like PepsiCo's Bubly momentum; Household & Personal Care at 40% +2.2% from laundry pods and eco-wipes reducing plastic by 25%, outpacing P&G's Tide Pods by 150 bps per IRI. Regionally, North America led at +2.4%, EMEA +1.5% via UK Tesco promotions, Asia-Pacific +0.5% despite India disruptions, Latin America +1.2%.

Price/mix added 3.4%, up 50 bps sequentially, from our AI-driven dynamic pricing averaging 4.2% hikes—modest versus Unilever and Colgate's 5-6%—with mix +1.2% from premiumization like Essentials Luxe personal care up 18% at 20% premium, organic trail mixes, and RTD coffees in the $15B functional bev segment per Euromonitor. Trade spend optimized 80 bps via SymphonyAI on high-ROI events. Regionally: NA +4.1%, EMEA +3.2%, APAC +2.8% with e-comm premium shift in China, LATAM +3.9% via EDLP. This balanced framework delivered 250 bps gross margin expansion.

On market share trends, we gained 110 basis points of value share globally per Nielsen, IRI, and Circana—our 11th straight quarter, outpacing categories 3x with 5.2% organic versus flat growth. Volume share +20 bps. In Personal Care (35% sales), +80 bps value to 18.2%, volume +50 bps from PureGlow clean beauty grabbing 200 bps from The Body Shop, DTC at 22%. Household +120 bps value to 22.4%, laundry pods +250 bps versus Tide. Beverages +60 bps from VitaFizz +300 bps in hydration. Snacks +90 bps from NutriCrunch +180 bps versus Kind. NA +140 bps, Europe +80 bps despite discounters, APAC +200 bps led by China, EM +90 bps. This from portfolio shaping, pricing analytics, AI forecasting at 92% accuracy.

Competitive activity was intense with P&G and Unilever upping trade spend to 22%, Tide Pods taking 1.5% NA laundry share. Private labels grew 4.8%. We responded with 18% trade budget on elastic promos recapturing 80 bps, Smart Price Architecture for 3% ROI uplift, 15 launches like EcoHydrate adding 150 bps, R&D at 2.8%, regional counters like AR try-on in APAC, CPG Nexus ERP cutting stockouts 22%, 65% renewable energy.

Geographically, developed markets (62% sales: NA, W. Europe, Japan/ANZ) grew 4.1% organic (2.8% volume, 1.3% price), NA 5.3% with PowerBrands +110 bps share, e-comm 18%; W. Europe 2.7% on eco-pods. Emerging (38%) surged 14.6% organic (9.2% volume, 5.4% price), India/ASEAN 22% via sachets to 85% rural ACV, China 18% e-comm 32%, LATAM 12%, MEA/EE 19%. Balanced Growth 2025 targets 4-6% developed CAGR, 12-15% emerging.

Our promotional strategy deployed $525M (12% gross revenue), up 6%, hitting 3.7x ROI versus 2.9% prior, cutting blunt EDLP 22%. TPRs 14% lift, TDx 4.2x ROI, digital 5.1x with personalized offers. NA 19% lift, EMEA 12%, APAC/LATAM 22%. Cut cannibalization 11%, net spend 8.2% versus peers.

Overall, Q3 net sales $15.2B up 7% organic, EPS $1.68 up 12%, gross margin +240 bps to 48.2% blended view from productivity $450M, segments: Beverages 4% volume, Snacks 9%, H&PC 6%. NA 8%, Europe 5%, APAC flat offset India, LATAM 10%. Win with Three: premiumize 42% sales, digitize 22% online, sustain 65% recycled packaging.

For outlook, Q4 organic 3.5-5.0% (2.0-2.5 price, 1.5-2.5 volume/mix), NA 4-5.5%, EMEA 2.5-4%, APAC 4.5-6%, LATAM flat-2%. FY25 4-6% organic implying $2-3.2B incremental on $48B base, segments Beauty 5-7%, Health 4.5-6.5%, Household 3-5%, Food/Bev 3.5-5.5. EPS $4.85-5.05, margins +100 bps to 18.5%. Risks: unemployment >4.2%, commodities, private labels; hedged 85% cocoa, essentials 45% sales.

This positions us strongly. Next, Taylor Kim will provide insights on our marketing and brand initiatives.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. Our brand building efforts have contributed significantly to our performance. We are seeing strong engagement across all our channels, especially with our new NovaGlow campaign, which has driven 15% uplift in brand equity scores through targeted social media and in-store experiences, aligning with premiumization and clean-label trends across personal care and snacks.

Following me, Morgan Patel will discuss supply chain performance.

Morgan Patel:
Thank you, Taylor. We continue to optimize our supply chain network and implement advanced technologies to improve efficiency and resilience, including AI-driven forecasting that boosted accuracy to 92% and reduced stockouts by 22%, alongside dual-sourcing 80% of key inputs and nearshoring to cut lead times 35%. We are also focused on reducing our carbon footprint, with 65% renewable energy across plants and 50% recycled packaging on track for 75% by 2025.

After Morgan, Riley Chen will share updates on our product innovation pipeline.

Riley Chen:
Thank you, Morgan. We are excited about our pipeline of innovative products. Our recent product launch, NutriCrunch high-protein bars with plant-based protein and clean ingredients, has been well-received by consumers, driving 180 bps share gains versus Kind and RXBAR, with 20 new SKUs in Q4 targeting functional nutrition and GLP-1 compatible options amid $50B market growth.

Finally, Casey Lopez will discuss our sales performance and channel strategy.

Casey Lopez:
Thank you, Riley. We are focused on expanding our distribution channels and improving our sales execution. We are seeing strong growth in our e-commerce channel, now 22% of sales up from 18%, with omnichannel yielding 2x NPS versus brick-and-mortar, plus 1,500 ACV points in club/mass for NovaClean and 95% ACV in convenience for snacks, alongside retail partnerships like Walmart and Amazon driving 15% comps.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for queuing questions: Press star then 1 on your touchtone phone. Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Johnson:
How is NovaCorp addressing the increasing demand for sustainable products?

Riley Chen:
Thanks, Mike. Sustainability is core to our innovation strategy. We've reformulated products like EcoShield pods and EcoHydrate drinks with 30% less plastic and 50% recycled PET, RSPO-certified 40% palm oil, and biodegradable wipes with 30% more eco-content targeting the $15B wipes market. Our Planet Positive platform has lifted brand equity 8 points, with green products showing +15% velocity per Kantar, and we're advancing regenerative ag with 500+ farmers to cut Scope 3 emissions 12%, ahead of peers.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan.

Lisa Chen:
What are your plans for expanding your presence in international markets?

Casey Lopez:
Great question, Lisa. Emerging markets are key to our growth, with 14.6% organic in Q3. We're targeting 12-15% CAGR via 500 localized SKUs like masala beverages in India, halal snacks in MEA, and beauty in China where e-comm is 32%. Capex $450M next year for cold-chain and plants in India/Indonesia/Vietnam cuts logistics 18%, boosting rural ACV to 85%. APAC led share gains +200 bps, LATAM +90 bps.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with Morgan Stanley.

David Patel:
Can you discuss the impact of inflation on your pricing strategy and consumer demand?

Jordan Lee:
Sure, David. Inflation remains a factor, with inputs up 15-20%, but our dynamic AI pricing from Black Book and SymphonyAI allowed modest 4.2% hikes minimizing erosion, contributing 3.4% to organic growth while expanding margins 250 bps. Volume +1.8% shows resilience, no material downtrading in essentials (45% sales). We're balancing recovery with value via EDLP in LATAM hyperinflation and hedging 85% cocoa. Q4 pricing 2-2.5 points, steady demand in premium/health.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emma Rodriguez with Barclays.

Emma Rodriguez:
How are you leveraging artificial intelligence to improve your supply chain efficiency?

Morgan Patel:
Emma, AI is transformative. Our NovaLogix and CPG Nexus with SAP Ariba/Snowflake predict elasticity, reduce spot buys 25%, hedge 70% volatiles, optimize manufacturing to 92% utilization yielding 8% COGS cuts in probiotics. Demand Forecaster at 92% accuracy cuts inventory 2-3 days, stockouts 22%, route optimization +22% distributor efficiency. Promo engine personalizes at ZIP level for 5x ROI pilots.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your insightful questions and participation. We are confident in our ability to deliver long-term sustainable growth and create value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaCorp Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
